hints: An empty linked stack is NULL. That is why every operation takes the top pointer and returns the (possibly new) top pointer.
PUSH is three lines: malloc, set key and next = s, return the new node. The new node becomes the head, so nothing else needs to move.
POP must save s->next into a local variable BEFORE calling free(s). Reading s->next after freeing s is use-after-free - it often appears to work, which is what makes it dangerous.
